entities.text: THIS 1:1 TECH POLICY SHOULDN’T BE HAPPENING TO OUR KIDS Francis Howell middle and high school students are required to take home district Chromebooks starting August 26 for FHN and carry them every single day. Extra weight in already heavy backpacks + more mandatory screen time is a direct hit on kids’ bodies and minds. Physical: Research consistently shows backpacks exceeding 10-15% of a student’s body weight increase neck, shoulder, and back pain plus postural problems. https://www.healthychildren.org/.../Backpack-Safety.aspx Emotional: Higher screen time is linked to increased anxiety and depression symptoms in adolescents. https://www.frontiersin.org/.../fpubh.2023.1101594/full Parents — push back. Email the Board of Education at board@fhsdschools.org and ask them to reconsider mandatory daily Chromebook carry and the added physical + emotional burden this places on students.

entities.text: PARENTS THE LONGER YOU WAIT and you don't hold your child's schools accountable gives these guys more time to dictate what's best for your child's physical mental and emotional health. Don’t be afraid to speak out for your kids because they are voiceless and rely on you. Parents — Know Your Rights You do not have to accept every lesson, survey, or program the school offers. Here’s what you can do: Opt out of any content that does not align with your family’s values or beliefs. You have the right to review materials and formally opt your child out. Opt out of surveys and questionnaires. Many are designed to collect personal information about your child’s beliefs, mental health, family life, or identity. You can refuse participation. Request to preview all surveys, social-emotional lessons, and sensitive materials before they are given to your child. Put everything in writing. Send a clear opt-out notice and keep a copy for your records. Stay informed and connected. Talk with other parents, attend school board meetings, and share information. Your child’s education and values start at home. You have the right — and the responsibility — to protect both.

entities.text: CARL DROPS THE MATH HAMMER ON PROP H Schooling the District on “Free Money” VOTE NO on Prop H The ballot will say $150 million. That’s only the face value of the bonds — not the real cost to taxpayers. We’ve seen this before. Prop S in 2020 said $244 million. The final price tag? $294 million. That’s $50 MILLION MORE than voters approved! How did they do it? They intentionally set higher-than-market interest rates so investors would pay a “premium.” The district got extra cash upfront. Taxpayers get stuck with higher interest payments for the next 10–20 years. The district will try to call that extra $50 million “free money.” There is no such thing as free money. It’s basic time value of money. The mathematics hasn’t changed. They can pick whatever number they want — they just need to be transparent about the true total cost. So far, they’re still refusing to do that. Until the district tells taxpayers the real maximum amount they’ll actually spend, Vote No on Prop H. Share this so more people know what’s really at stake. Listen to common sense Carl >>> https://www.youtube.com/live/gXJwYo-H72c...

Please take time to review the district’s online library catalog and identify any titles you want your child opted out of: Francis Howell Destiny Library Search: https://fhsdschools.follettdestiny.com Knowledge is power. Stay informed and stay involved.

entities.text: 1:1 TECHNOLOGY IS COMING TO ALL FHSD MIDDLE & HIGH SCHOOLS Every middle and high school student gets their own take-home Chromebook this fall. Elementary stays with classroom carts. IF IT SOUNDS TOO GOOD TO BE TRUE… IT IS. DO THEY REALLY THINK WE’RE THAT STUPID? The district says this will “save $300,000 a year.” Reality check: • Damage & loss rates jump when devices go home every day (8–12% annually) • Hardware is only ~25% of the real cost — repairs, IT support, and replacements eat the rest • Other districts have spent tens of millions fixing broken Chromebooks that only last 2–3 years • Parents still get hit with repair/replacement fees They also claim “no more screen time.” Giving every middle & high schooler a personal device makes that hard to believe. More screens. Higher long-term costs. This is not a win for students or taxpayers. CONTACT: board@fhsdschools.org

entities.text: BOOK ALERT The book: Amazons, Abolitionists, and Activists: A Graphic History of Women’s Fight for Their Rights by Mikki Kendall Library: Francis Howell Central Is marketed as a history of women’s rights. In reality, it is a progressive, intersectional feminist narrative that reframes the entire story through modern identity politics. It uses a classroom framing device to walk readers through history while pushing a clear ideological agenda. This book contains: • Explicit inclusion of LGBTQ rights and gender ideology as core parts of “women’s rights” • Promotion of reproductive rights / abortion as a central women’s issue • Intersectional framing that elevates race and identity politics above classical equality or biblical views of men and women • Criticism of early women’s suffrage leaders (including white feminists) for not being progressive enough on race and other modern causes • A strong call to ongoing leftist-style activism presented as the natural continuation of the fight for rights • Adult political content delivered in an accessible graphic novel format aimed at teens If your child is in Francis Howell Central and checking out graphic histories, this is one worth previewing yourself. Not every book with “women’s rights” in the title is teaching the same values. IMPORTANT FOR PARENTS: If you do NOT want your child to have access to this type of content at school, you must contact your school's media specialist (librarian) or your child's principal. Written notification is required. Without it, your child will have full access to any book the school deems appropriate, even material such as this. You can also: • Request a list of books your child has already checked out. • Sign up to receive daily email notifications of every book your child checks out. These options are available at both the elementary and secondary levels. I've said this before, and I'll say it again: we no longer live in an age where adults are protecting children from sexual content. We are living in an age where adults are offering minor children books with age-inappropriate sexual content under the guise of education. I will never stop fighting for our children because every single one of them are worth fighting for! entities.text: DEAR EXHAUSTED TEACHERS Some exhaustion is self imposed. Ask yourself is the exhaustion you’re experiencing a direct result of stepping far outside your professional lane? Your job is to teach core subjects — not to promote or encourage any particular lifestyle, sexual identity, or ideology to other people’s children. Stay in your lane as an educator, respect parental rights, and don’t exhaust yourself. *** This teacher was found to maintain an in-classroom PRIDE library at Hollenbeck. Parents deserve transparency: Will those same books and ideology follow them to their new position at Bryan Middle School? *** PARENTS HAVE THE RIGHT TO KNOW. Email: ryan.johnson@fhsdschools.org Bryan Middle Principal

entities.text: The U.S. Department of Justice and the U.S. Department of Education announced they will pursue enforcement action against Kansas City, Kansas Public Schools, alleging the district violated federal parental-rights and student-privacy laws by shielding students' transgender status from parents. Federal investigators pointed to a district policy stating that school staff "should not disclose information that may reveal a student's transgender status or gender nonconforming presentation to others, including parents." The Education Department's Student Privacy Policy Office opened its investigation in August 2025; in April 2026, it found the district's policy violated the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act, and in June it issued a formal Letter of Impending Enforcement Action after also finding a Title IX violation. Read more in the comments....

entities.text: FERPA Opt-Out Reminder for FHSD Families Did you know? FERPA allows schools to share certain "directory information" (such as a student's name, grade level, honors, activities, or photos) unless a parent/guardian chooses to opt out. You may want to opt out if you prefer that your student's information and/or photos not be included in school publications, websites, social media, yearbooks, news releases, or other approved communications. FHSD Public Notices & FERPA Opt-Out Information: https://www.fhsdschools.org/public-notices Opt Out Form: https://resources.finalsite.net/.../FERPA-and-Media-Opt... Please review the information carefully to determine what is best for your family.

entities.text: FHSD Board Member Sara Dillard at Pride St. Charles (June 20, 2026) Sara Dillard, elected to the Francis Howell School District Board of Education in April 2026, shared this photo from the Pride St. Charles event. —>> SHE IS PICTURED WEARING HER OFFICIAL FRANCIS HOWELL SCHOOL DISTRICT NAME TAG WHILE ATTENDING <<— the event, which featured prominent rainbow and progress pride flags in the background. As a public school board member, this raises questions about personal advocacy and how it aligns with maintaining viewpoint neutrality in district policies, curriculum, and school environments that SERVE ALL FAMILIES. Wearing her official district name tag creates the appearance that FHSD endorses the event. District policies require viewpoint neutrality — personal views should not be presented as official school positions. This raises serious questions about policy violations and potential grounds for FORMAL REVIEW and DISMISSAL! What are your thoughts on elected officials participating in these events while representing the district? entities.text: FHSD Parents & Taxpayers: Questions on the New “No Tax Rate Increase” Props O & H Headed to November The Board just voted to put two propositions on the November 3, 2026 ballot that they’re marketing as “no-tax-rate-increase” measures. Here’s the quick breakdown: Proposition O – Levy Transfer Shifts 12.5 cents from the debt service levy to the operating levy. The district says this will add roughly $5.5 million per year to the operating budget (for salaries, buses, food service, etc.) without raising your overall tax rate. They cite a ~$9.3 million state funding shortfall over the next two years plus rising costs for labor, insurance, fuel, and supplies. Proposition H – $150 Million Bond Issue For “critical facility needs” across all 23 schools — roofs, windows, HVAC, mechanical/electrical systems, safety & security, CTE programs, ADA compliance, sidewalks, parking lots, and athletic/performing arts spaces. Also pitched as no tax rate increase. I have some real questions about these: • For Prop O: Is there really a $9M+ state funding shortfall hitting us this hard right now? What’s the actual story behind the funding formula changes? We need the full, transparent picture — not just the headline number. • For Prop H: It’s interesting they don’t say what will happen to our current bond levy rate if this does NOT pass. Would it actually go down once existing obligations are paid off? And did they have to do any maneuvering or creative structuring to get this labeled a true “no tax increase” bond issue? This comes right after our Prop S experience. What started as a $240 million bond ended up adding another $150 million in costs (totaling around $390 million) because it wasn’t planned or executed right the first time. We can’t keep repeating that pattern. Transparency on these big fiscal moves matters. Our kids, our teachers, and our community deserve straight answers and better planning before we head to the polls. See the attached PDF from the recent board meeting update for the details they released. https://go.boarddocs.com/mo/fhsdmo/Board.nsf/Public# https://www.fhsdschools.org/.../distric.../post/prop-o-and-h What do you think? Do these questions matter to you too? Have you looked at the numbers? Drop your thoughts in the comments — and keep pushing for real accountability. Share this if you believe more FHSD families should see it. #FHSD #FrancisHowell #PropO #PropH #SchoolBond #TaxTransparency #StCharlesCounty

Our kids need more real teaching and fewer distractions — not expensive tech experiments that harm learning. Back to basics works. Let’s hold FHSD accountable! entities.text: Taxpayers, the Missouri State Auditor’s report on the Francis Howell School District’s superintendent hiring debacle with Dr. Mike Dominguez exposes wasted money and weak leadership. The district paid a search firm over $40,000 — yet we’ve never been refunded despite the $229k+ payout to a superintendent who never started. Some have said Board President Steven Blair was tasked with pursuing that refund. He allegedly heard “no,” tucked his tail, and backed down. Why does Steven Blair run to the lawyers for every move? Is this the passive leadership we want protecting our wallets? Real accountability means demanding better — not rolling over. Parents deserve board members who fight for fiscal responsibility. entities.text: SPORTS FORM: HOW DOES YOUR CHILD IDENTIFY? Did you know that the sports physical forms required for Missouri kids to play school team sports come from MSHSAA (Missouri State High School Activities Association)? These standard forms now include the question: “How does your child identify?” In no way, shape, or form should “identifies as” belong on a sports physical form. It should be sex assigned at birth — period! This is about protecting fair competition and common sense. Contact the MSHSAA Board today and voice your concerns. • Jim Welby (St. Louis) — jwelby@stdominichs.org • email@mshsaa.org Or what’s next… boys competing in girls sports and vice versa? Parents — it’s time to speak up now.

entities.text: MORE TAX LEVIES COMING SOON? The full liberal FHSD school board says it’s never enough During the Prop RT fight, they warned of massive cuts (even threatening disability programs) if the tax freeze passed. Now that it failed — and they didn’t lose the $4M they claimed — they’re suddenly highlighting: • “No-Tax-Increase Debt Service Levy Transfer” • “No-Tax-Increase Bond Issue” So there are ways to shift money without a big tax hike? Why the scare tactics then (like threatening the Defunding the Disability program)? Taxpayers deserve straight answers, not selective urgency. The Result: Prevents Tax Relief You (and future homeowners) pay the current debt tax rate for many more years — often 10–20+ extra years. That adds up to thousands per homeowner over time. What do you think, FHSD families & St. Charles taxpayers? Stay tuned to board meetings. https://www.youtube.com/live/m_2hc5G4eCo?si=H5AOB8wP9h8rAUPP #FrancisHowell #PropRT #SchoolFunding

entities.text: HAPPY PARENTAL RIGHTS MONTH! On June 1, 1925, the U.S. Supreme Court issued one of the most important parental rights decisions in American history: Pierce v. Society of Sisters. The Court affirmed a principle that still matters today: "The child is not the mere creature of the State." More than a century later, parents across the country continue to advocate for a voice in their children's education and future. As we celebrate Parental Rights Month, consider supporting the work of educating, equipping, and engaging parents nationwide. Thanks to a generous partner, every donation made through June 30 will be matched dollar-for-dollar up to $40,000. https://www.momsforliberty.org/june-26-matching-grant/ #ParentalRightsMonth #WeTheParents #Moms4Liberty

entities.text: WHERE DO YOU DRAW THE LINE? Public schools should educate—not indoctrinate. • Flying sexual flags endorses adult ideologies that contradict the faith of many Christian families. • Stocking libraries with sexual and vulgar books for all ages exposes kids to inappropriate content. • Hiding books in classroom libraries keeps parents in the dark. • Threatening lawsuits to allow boys in girls’ or girls’ in boys locker rooms and restrooms violates privacy, safety, and fairness. The line is simple: Age-appropriate academics, full transparency with parents, and basic biological reality. Schools serve children and families—not activist agendas. Demand curriculum review, parental notification, and neutral education. Your voice matters.

entities.text: ARREST MADE: Fox Middle School teacher, Zachery Robert Leonard, 42, of St. Louis has been arrested and charged following an investigation into inappropriate sexual and criminal conduct involving a student under 14. Arnold Detectives along with School Resource Officers began an immediate investigation after the incident was reported on 5/6/2026. Leonard was initially arrested on 5/6/2026 but released as Detectives continued to gather evidence. On 5/11/2026 Detectives submitted a Probable Cause Statement to the Prosecuting Attorney's Office. On 5/14/2026 a No Bond Warrant was issued for Leonard's arrest and Arnold Detectives were able to locate and take him into custody without incident. Leonard has been charged with Enticement of a Child, (2x) Child Molestation 3rd Degree, and (2x) Sexual Contact w/ Student. Leonard is currently being held at the Arnold Police Department Jail without bond. We would like to thank the Fox-C6 School District for their cooperation and assistance with this investigation. We would also like to thank the Jefferson County Prosecuting Attorney's Office for moving quickly to file charges in this case. Our priority is the safety and protection of children in our community. The actions alleged in this case represent a serious breach of trust and we will continue to work closely with prosecutors to ensure accountability.

entities.text: TRANSPARENCY ISN’T HARASSMENT. PARENTAL INVOLVEMENT ISN’T EXTREMISM. If you classify bringing the TRUTH about what’s actually happening in your child’s classroom as “harassment,” then you’ve got a serious misconception about what harassment actually is. Sharing proof, of what’s being recommended or provided isn’t bullying — it’s called being an involved parent. It’s called transparency. It’s called PROTECTING KIDS and YOUR PARENTAL RIGHTS. Real harassment is trying to silence parents who dare to look inside the classroom and speak up about what they find. Real harassment is treating moms and dads like enemies for simply letting other parents know what their children are being taught and influenced. If we can’t agree on that basic principle, we’ve lost our way. What do you think — is speaking truth in your child’s education protected, or is it being twisted into something it’s not? Drop your thoughts below. #ParentalRights #EducationTransparency #KnowWhatsInTheClassroom #FHSD #FrancisHowell

entities.text: The Missouri NEA (teachers’ union) sued the state of Missouri. They tried to stop $50+ million in public tax money from going to the MOScholars program — a scholarship that helps certain kids (especially those with disabilities or from low-income families) pay for private school, homeschooling, tutoring, or therapy. The NEA argued the funding was done the wrong way (unconstitutional) and would hurt public schools. The judge dismissed the lawsuit completely. He ruled the NEA didn’t have the legal right to sue in this way, and even if they did, the funding was legal. The money can keep flowing to the scholarships.

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Becky Hormuth and her transgender son, Levi, thought they were protected after a Missouri law banning transition-related care for minors took effect in August. The law grandfathered in those who had already been receiving puberty blockers or hormone therapy prior to Aug. 28, meaning they, in theory, would be able to continue their treatment. However, the hospital where Levi had been receiving care informed patients in September that it would no longer be providing such care, citing the “unsustainable liability” the law creates for health care professionals, as it allows providers of transition-related care for minors to be sued by their patients. “We both just sat and cried together on the floor of his bedroom,” Becky said of the reaction she and Levi had upon hearing the news. “He connected with those doctors, and they’re like family to us — they know him personally. His big worry was, ‘Who’s going to help me now?’” ​​More than 500 state bills targeting lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and queer people have been introduced in 2023, according to a tally by the American Civil Liberties Union. Of those bills, 75 became law, according to an NBC News analysis of the ACLU’s data. Read more: nbcnews.app.link/xHnIJsCtDFb | 2vuM3UQjKU.com

entities.text: Move St. Charles County School Board Elections to November for Higher Turnout￼ Missouri Senate Bill 1002 would move St. Charles County school board elections and tax increase votes to the November general election for much higher voter turnout. Sponsored by Senator Adam Schnelting, the bill has passed the Senate and is now in the House. Why this is a win for parents and taxpayers: • April 7 turnout was only 19% — a tiny fraction of voters decided the entire Francis Howell School Board. • November elections typically see 60-70%+ turnout, giving everyday families a real voice instead of letting special interests dominate. - For example special interests (including teachers’ unions like the MNEA/NEA) are actively organizing to kill the bill so they can keep low-turnout April elections that favor organized special interests. • School board decisions affect our kids and millions in taxes — they deserve broad community input, not low-turnout insider control. • This puts power back where it belongs: with parents and taxpayers. This isn’t partisanship — it’s basic democracy and accountability. =============================== Call or email your Missouri State Representative TODAY and tell them to SUPPORT SB 1002. =============================== Always include your full address to confirm you’re a constituent. • Tricia Byrnes (District 63 – Wentzville area)�Email: Tricia.Byrnes@house.mo.gov�Phone: (573) 751-1460 • Deanna Self (District 64 – parts of O’Fallon, St. Paul, etc.)�Email: Deanna.Self@house.mo.gov�Phone: (573) 751-1484 • Wendy Hausman (District 65 – St. Peters, Cottleville, parts of St. Charles)�Email: Wendy.Hausman@house.mo.gov�Phone: (573) 751-3717 • Scott Miller (District 69 – additional St. Charles County areas overlapping FHSD)�Email: Scott.Miller@house.mo.gov�Phone: (573) 751-5365 • Terri Violet (District 104 – parts of St. Charles County / FHSD)�Email: Terri.Violet@house.mo.gov • Travis Wilson (District 106 – St. Charles area)�Use the contact form on house.mo.gov/MemberDetails.aspx?district=106 (no public direct email listed). • CC - adam.schnelting@senate.mo.gov, nick.schroer@senate.mo.gov

We owe it to our children to choose universities that prioritize education over ideology. Do your homework on campus culture, viewpoint diversity, and what students are actually learning. What schools are you considering (or avoiding) for your kids? —our children’s future depends on it. #CollegeChoices #HigherEducation #ParentalResponsibility

entities.text: Wentzville School District Settles Transgender Bathroom Lawsuit with Missouri AG Great news for transparency and parental rights in Wentzville R-IV Schools! The district has reached a settlement with Attorney General Catherine Hanaway, resolving a 2023 Sunshine Law case. The board was accused of discussing a transgender student bathroom and locker room access policy in closed sessions (June 2023) instead of openly with the public. Key points of the April 2026 agreement: • No admission of wrongdoing by the district • Acknowledges parents’ fundamental right to know about and participate in decisions affecting their children’s education, safety, and welfare • Commits to full compliance with Missouri’s Open Meetings/Sunshine Law • Requires Sunshine Law training for board members and staff • Must post a public statement about the case and settlement on the district website This reinforces that important school policies should be debated in the open, not behind closed doors. Full settlement: https://ago.mo.gov/.../State-v.-Wentzville-Settlement... What do you think—transparency wins? Share your thoughts!

entities.text: Judge Requires Parental Notification for Elementary School Gender Lessons A book called “My Shadow is PINK” Brave fifth-grader Shea Encinas stood up to his California school after they forced him to read the book My Shadow Is Pink and teach gender identity lessons to a kindergartner—without allowing his family to opt out. Despite their Christian beliefs being ignored, Shea and his parents fought back… and won! The Encinitas Union School District has now dropped its appeal, meaning SCHOOLS MUST GIVE PARENTS ADVANCE NOTICE and the right to OPT their kids OUT of such content. This is a powerful victory for parental rights and religious freedom! Link to article: https://www.californiafamily.org/.../victory-for-parents.../ YouTube interview: https://youtu.be/mdv5LhmLTvg?si=W0cpdH9dSgg0YDqv #ParentalRights #ProtectOurKids #MyShadowIsPink #StandForFaith @firstlibertyinstitute

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | The Supreme Court has ruled that parents cannot be forced to have their young children participate in school lessons that conflict with their sincerely held religious beliefs. The Court said schools must allow families to opt their children out of certain elementary classroom materials involving LGBTQ themes when those materials contradict their faith. The case arose after a Maryland school district removed opt-out options and stopped notifying parents about the content being taught. The ruling does not ban the material itself, but it affirms a foundational principle: parents — not the state — have the primary responsibility for directing the moral and religious upbringing of their children. Schools may teach these topics, but they cannot compel participation from students whose families object on religious grounds. | TtVyVL.com

entities.text: Teacher wins $650,000 lawsuit after refusing to use trans students’ preferred pronouns A former Indiana music teacher has been awarded a $650,000 settlement following a long-running legal dispute with his school district over classroom pronoun use. The case began in 2017 when the teacher said his religious beliefs prevented him from using students’ preferred pronouns, leading to a policy conflict with school administrators and eventually a civil rights lawsuit. In response, the teacher adopted a last-name-only approach for all students as a compromise. However, some students reported feeling singled out and uncomfortable, prompting the school district to withdraw the arrangement. The disagreement escalated, ultimately resulting in the teacher’s resignation and years of legal proceedings over claims of religious discrimination. The settlement concludes a seven-year case that has drawn national attention to the balance between religious rights and student inclusion in schools. The outcome reflects ongoing legal debates in the United States over how institutions handle conflicts between personal beliefs and policies designed to support diverse student identities. #fblifestyle #photography #community #Education #LegalCase #USSchools References: BBC News: Coverage on education and religious rights cases Reuters: Reports on US civil rights and school disputes CNN: Analysis of pronoun policies in schools Fox News: Legal updates on education-related lawsuits

entities.text: All this outrage about schools, fire, libraries, and disability programs losing funding seems to show up only when taxpayers ask questions and say no more taxes we are tapped out. •Where is that same outrage when developers receive tax abatements and incentives that divert revenue away from our same districts? • St. Charles County’s 2024 incentive report confirms Chapter 100 and Chapter 353 abatements reduce or redirect tax dollars from schools and other local taxing authorities. • In WSD, the 2023 agreement tied to the Bryan Road/Highway N and Feise/Bryan developments includes abatement of real property taxes, with only a $50,000 annual contribution (2024–2036) instead of full taxation. But we just keep building, thousands of new homes and apartments: The Solstice The Sullivan (LSL) New Town expansion (St Charles) Shady Creek (Hwy N) Autumn Hollows (Hwy N) Creekside at Sommers (45 homes across LHS) Inverness (Bryan & Feise) The Prairie & Prairie Encore (190 apartments) Trailside Farms (Hwy N toward LSL) • Are these developments paying their full share, or are incentives shifting that burden to the community? When local officials approve these deals, they are choosing to reduce or delay full tax collections through abatements and other agreements. • Why do developers get tax breaks, while the families already living here pay the increases every year? Before asking taxpayers for more and more money, there should be accountability, transparency, and better long-term planning.

entities.text: THINK SHEET FIX; I THINK NOT At the March 19 Board meeting, teachers laid it out: skyrocketing student behaviors with ZERO consequences, safety threats, physical aggression, insane workloads (especially SPED), staff shortages, and zero trust in leadership. Their “fix” for the discipline crisis? A “think sheet” so kids can sit and reflect on what they did wrong. Wow… can’t make this stuff up. Legit question: Who exactly are we adding to the payroll to babysit and hand out these magic reflection worksheets? Our kids deserve real safety and real accountability — not worksheets. Parents, if this concerns you, comment below and show up at the next Board meeting! AND… * * * VOTE APRIL 7 * * * for the first three on the ballot…. 1. PUSZKAR 2. GREENWOOD 3. JAWORSKI #FHSDParents #SchoolSafety #DisciplineNow #ThinkSheetFix

entities.text: Parents of Francis Howell – please show up tonight for the Board Meeting! Even with many challenges, age-inappropriate books are still in our libraries, and Policy 6310 is making it nearly impossible for parents to protect our children from explicit material. We need your voices at public comments! The Workplace Culture Survey results and the vote on the new Safe Schools Curriculum are pushing further into the gender ideology movement — the wrong decision for our students and for parents trying to uphold their religious and moral beliefs. If you’re a Christian, conservative, or simply care about protecting our children, stand up and speak out. Support Jane Puszkar Jane Puszkar, FHSD Board of Education as she continues to fight for what’s right for our kids! Attend in person or watch live on the Francis Howell YouTube channel. Your presence matters now more than ever! YouTube Channel (for live-streaming tonight’s Board meeting and all others): https://www.youtube.com/@francishowellschooldistric9240 Patron Comments Sign-Up (to speak at tonight’s meeting): https://www.fhsdschools.org/.../patron-comments-sign-ups This page links directly to the Google sign-up form (opens 24 hours before meetings) and the live speaker list (Google Sheet that refreshes every 5 minutes).

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Quick Preview of Tonight’s March Board Meeting. 1-We will have elementary students leading our Pledge of Allegiance. 2-We will celebrate a Barnwell Robotics Team for winning State. 3-We will approve and sign the negotiated contract with our teachers union FHEA. 4-We will vote to approve accepting bids for different pavement and roofing projects. 5-We will listen to the results of our Workplace Culture Survey and discuss next steps to make Francis Howell better for everyone. 6-We will have a second reading and vote on Policy 6310, which largely refers to the standards we use when purchasing books for the Libraries. Note: Parents have and will continue to have the power to choose the books they want their students to be able to access. 7-We will vote on a Safe Schools Curriculum developed by FHSD that is connected to K-12 Missouri Learning Standards. 8- We will have our monthly finance report where we see the big picture financial health of the district. This report will include information for board members about the possible loss of $4 million in Year One and $54 million loss over five years if Prop RT passes. You are welcome to join us tonight or watch us online at our Francis Howell YouTube channel. | ceagHei.com

entities.text: Many False claims out there that the sky is falling in regards to Prop RT. Prop RT only freezes future tax hikes—it doesn’t defund the school or specifically special-needs services. They found $78M for an over-budget high school + $230K for a no-show superintendent. Manage existing money first. Still short? Seek transparent new tax hikes taxpayers deserve to know where their money is going.

entities.text: PRIVATE PRIDE Libraries In Classrooms I recently discovered “private pride libraries” in our 7th grade English class at Hollenbeck Middle School. Some of these books were not found in the library commons, so they appear to be in direct violation of the In-Classroom Library Policy (under 6310/6341). This policy requires all books to be provided in a list to the Board for review and prohibits bringing in books not already in the district library. This isn’t happening — unauthorized books are everywhere, the superintendent knows, and nothing’s being done. This also violates my rights as a parent, as I am unable to monitor or consent to what my child is reading in class. Violation Scenario If a classroom library includes books not reported or approved via the Learning Commons process, the teacher (or district) is in violation: • They bypassed the required transparency steps, since new titles aren’t disclosed to the Board. • They may also be subject to challenges under Policy 6341, which treats classroom and school library materials identically. [go.boarddocs.com] – Please email your concerns to Board@fhsdschools.org #SchoolTransparency #ParentalRights #FHSD #FrancisHowell #AgeAppropriateEducation

entities.text: SHINY NEW TECH I feel this view oversimplifies the 1:1 Chromebook push at our schools and skips key details. Valid Concerns: 1. Device Shortfalls: They’re underestimating needs—ignoring breakage, theft, or loss. We’ll need way more than the initial estimate! 2. Tech Support Gap: No plans to add to the 25 Tech Aids or place them in schools. Teachers will end up as IT fixers, stealing time from teaching. 3. Unclear Usage: Just “strategic teaching” as the reason? No details on apps, integration, or curriculum fit. 4. Data Privacy Missing: Zero policies on protecting student info from third parties. Big red flag in today’s world! 5. Budget Blues: $1M per year for devices (totaling $5M over 5 years) + $2.3M for infrastructure (accounting for e-rate reimbursement, but they haven’t even received the last one requested). Both estimates are lowballs, and they ignore costs for increased staffing, infrastructure upgrades, device losses, blue light glasses to protect students’ eyes, or extra tech support. What about the fiscal cliff? 6. Internet Upgrades Needed: Current network probably won’t cut it—upgrades are essential, but are they fully planned? Bottom line: The pitch was all about buying/deploying, ignoring academic pros/cons. The current proposal covers only middle and high schools (not elementary). Feels like “keeping up with other districts” vibes from 2 years ago. Aside from all this info… what is the reason we are even looking to do this? Are there lots of students that don’t have access to a laptop at home? Wouldn’t it be more economical to only supply those in need? There is no way that just because the personal model is said to cost less than the classroom, that it’s going to cost less in total in the long run. It’s just not possible. This absolutely sets students up for more screen time. Have you seen the negative impacts on that? Back to the question: What problem are we trying to solve? Let’s discuss real student and taxpayer impacts!

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | I have heard some misconceptions from Thursday BOE Technology Update. We currently use a classroom approach to distribute chromebooks to high school and middle school students. This does require each classroom to have a higher number of chromebooks to match the hour with the largest class size. We are shifting to a personal chromebook model where each high school and middle school student will be assigned their own chromebook. Thursday’s Technology Update included these advantages to the change. 1- Money Savings - The personal chromebook model costs less than the classroom model. 2- Students can bring their personal chromebook home allowing for greater access to homework and Canva. 3- Students can more easily navigate the chromebook, as shared by Thursday’s student representative. This change in distribution does not mean students will be on technology more than before. It is simply a change in how chromebooks are assigned. This change provides greater efficiency for students and saves money for taxpayers. Win-Win. Transparency is only effective if it is connected to open, understandable communication. I hope this helps. Please feel free to ask questions. I’ll do my best to answer them. | FUv4pt.com

Tech Support Gap: No plans to add to the 25 Tech Aids or place them in schools. Teachers will end up as IT fixers, stealing time from teaching. 3. Unclear Usage: Just “strategic teaching” as the reason? No details on apps, integration, or curriculum fit. 4. Data Privacy Missing: Zero policies on protecting student info from third parties. Big red flag in today’s world! 5. Budget Blues: $1M per year for devices (totaling $5M over 5 years) + $2.3M for infrastructure (accounting for e-rate reimbursement, but they haven’t even received the last one requested). Both estimates are lowballs, and they ignore costs for increased staffing, infrastructure upgrades, device losses, blue light glasses to protect students’ eyes, or extra tech support. What about the fiscal cliff? 6. Internet Upgrades Needed: Current network probably won’t cut it—upgrades are essential, but are they fully planned? Bottom line: The pitch was all about buying/deploying, ignoring academic pros/cons. The current proposal covers only middle and high schools (not elementary). Feels like “keeping up with other districts” vibes from 2 years ago. Aside from all this info… what is the reason we are even looking to do this? Are there lots of students that don’t have access to a laptop at home? Wouldn’t it be more economical to only supply those in need? There is no way that just because the personal model is said to cost less than the classroom, that it’s going to cost less in total in the long run. It’s just not possible. This absolutely sets students up for more screen time. Have you seen the negative impacts on that? Back to the question: What problem are we trying to solve? Let’s discuss real student and taxpayer impacts!

entities.text: Hey Missouri families and educators! Lt. Gov. David Wasinger just launched the “Lieutenant Governor’s Award for American Patriotism” essay contest to celebrate America’s 250th anniversary and inspire patriotism in our kids. Open to all Missouri students in grades K-12. Write a letter using one of these prompts: • “I am proud to be an American because…” • “I love America because…” Word count limits: • Grades K-3: 50 words • Grades 4-6: 100 words • Grades 7-12: 200 words Submission deadline: Entries must be postmarked no later than March 1, 2026. Winners will be honored at a special ceremony and lunch at the Missouri State Capitol on June 26, 2026, where they’ll read their letters aloud! This is a great way for kids to reflect on our nation’s blessings of liberty, faith, family, and freedom. Get those entries in soon—spread the word! For full details: https://ltgov.mo.gov/lieutenant-governor-david-wasinger.../ Project requirements PDF: https://ltgov.mo.gov/.../Letters-to-Lt.-Governor-Project...

entities.text: Student Walk out UPDATE- Email from the district: let’s hope they follow their own rules February 12, 2026 FHN families: Some FHN students made the decision to leave their classes after 3rd period and walk out of the school building. FHN administrators are with the students and are directing students to move to a supervised location on campus. We are being told the walkout is a demonstration against recent actions by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The District has provided guidance to all schools for navigating student protests. Our ultimate goal is to maintain a safe and secure school campus and to ensure that students do not present a major disruption to the learning environment. Here is some information about how we respond to student walkouts. We do not dismiss schools for walkouts, peaceful protests, or other demonstrations. Students who choose to participate in the walkout will be under adult supervision while on campus. Students will receive absence marks based on their actual attendance in each class, and they will face consequences for non-attendance or tardiness consistent with our normal procedures. Instruction will continue as scheduled. Students will not be given additional time to complete quizzes or exams that may be given during the walkout. Should a walkout happen during lunch, students who choose to participate will not be granted additional lunchtime. Consistent with MSHSAA bylaws and the FHSD Activities Handbook, students must attend school the entire day, or be marked excused by the principal, in order to participate in practices, rehearsals, or games for athletic teams or performance groups. Any verbal escalations, inappropriate behaviors, altercations, or other actions stemming from participation in the walkout will be subject to disciplinary action in accordance with the FHSD Code of Student Conduct. Students will be instructed to return to class as soon as the walkout concludes. Members of the media or general public wishing to observe or participate in the student-led walkout will not be permitted on campus during the instructional day. The principal has the authority to temporarily limit all traffic in and out, including parents and visitors, to protect student safety. Administrators and counselors will be available to assist students in processing their emotions. Every effort will be made to be consistent in our guidelines and consequences. The same policies and Code of Student Conduct that govern our work every day will also apply during any student walkouts. Thank you for helping us maintain safe learning environments for all students. FHN Admin Team

entities.text: WALKOUT HAPPENING NOW! Students at Francis Howell North are currently participating in a walkout right now. Reports say at least 50+ kids have left class to protest (details on the exact cause are still unclear—some are speculating it could be related to ICE/immigration enforcement, but it might not be. No official confirmation yet). This is happening DURING school hours, unlike Fort Zumwalt where similar things were organized AFTER school. Will these students be held responsible? Will there be absences marked, detentions, or other consequences like in past walkouts? Or will the district look the other way? Superintendent Mark Delaney hasn’t responded yet with any official statement (as far as I know), but this seems disruptive to the school day. Anyone have more details or eyewitness accounts? #FrancisHowellNorth #FHN #Walkout #StudentProtest

entities.text: Following district policy is not harassment. Raising concerns about age-appropriate content is not hate. Disagreeing does not justify abuse. What kind of learning community responds to concerns with intimidation and name-calling? Just a sample of threats and what I’ve been called during this process: • “Most recently, I was labeled a “faux (fake) Christian,” “white,” “heterosexual,” and warned “don’t screw up my kids’ diversity” • “They mess with one of our kids, they mess with all of us” • “Dimwitted” • “bully/intimidate/cause trouble” • “Toxic candidate” • “Book banning is for dummies” • “Anti-intellectual” • “Mouth breather” • “Idiot” • “Racist” • “Illiterate” • “Not competent to read” • “Children shouldn’t suffer for the sins of their parents” • “Stupid” • “People in green/wood houses shouldn't throw stones” • “living in glass houses, mind-bogglingly unaware of their own children's reality” This is deeply concerning, and it needs to be said. I have not attacked or harassed anyone. I have raised documented, firsthand concerns regarding my child’s 7th grade English class at Hollenbeck and both of my children’s school libraries. The irony is clear: this ‘learning community’—including the teacher herself—has exposed her identity far more than I ever did. Attacking my religion in response is inappropriate and reflects clear hypocrisy rather than engagement with the issue. This should concern every parent. Given this, I now question whether I should be the one issuing cease-and-desist letters sighting harassment, misrepresentations, extreme emotional distress, damage to my reputation. Would that take the focus off the kids? Because the focus hasn’t been on kids at all—it’s been on adult agendas/identities.

entities.author: School Watchlist is with State Senator Nick Schroer.
entities.text: Francis Howell Parents — Momentum is on our side! This week, the Eighth Circuit Court of Appeals delivered a major win for parents and taxpayers. The court ruled that authors and publishers do not have a right to force sexually explicit materials into public school libraries. The case involved Iowa’s SF 496, which requires age-appropriate books and removes materials depicting sex acts. The court made it clear: • The First Amendment does not guarantee any book at taxpayer expense. • Removing explicit content is not a “book ban.” Missouri parents, it’s time to act. Age-inappropriate and sexually explicit materials still don’t belong in our kids’ schools — especially in elementary and middle grades. Contact our St. Charles County senators today and urge them to introduce or support strong legislation like Iowa’s SF 496 (and back SB 483 sponsored by Sen. Nick Schroer to protect kids from explicit sexual material): Use the email draft below. The more voices, the stronger the message. Our kids’ innocence and education come first. Share with other FHSD parents! #FrancisHowell #ProtectOurKids #ParentalRights #SB483 ———————————————————————— Email Draft (Copy & Paste Ready) To: adam.schnelting@senate.mo.gov, nick.schroer@senate.mo.gov Subject: Remove Age-Inappropriate Materials from Missouri Schools Dear Senator Schnelting and Senator Schroer, I am a parent in the Francis Howell School District in St. Charles County. I urge you to champion legislation similar to Iowa’s SF 496 and to support SB 483 (sponsored by Sen. Schroer) to strengthen protections against explicit sexual material in schools. Recent rulings, including this week’s Eighth Circuit decision, confirm that schools have the authority and responsibility to keep age-inappropriate books — especially those depicting or describing sex acts — out of classrooms and libraries, particularly for K-6 students. Parents deserve transparency and the right to protect their children’s innocence. Taxpayer-funded schools should focus on education, not exposing kids to explicit content. Please take the lead on this issue in the next legislative session. I would appreciate any update on your plans to protect Missouri families. Thank you for your strong advocacy for St. Charles County families. Sincerely,

entities.text: Some experiences show it might be fostering division among kids: (These are my recent experiences) • At the Rec Plex pool, young black boys (around age 10) said to each other, white swimmers should clear a lane “because it’s Black History Month.” • My daughter’s biracial friend texted a group chat to the white friends “so what you guys gonna be doing for me since it’s black history month”, or it means they don’t care. And “you guys didn’t go through what we had to”. • A new Black student was seen texting “I hate all these white people at this school”. These moments highlight a growing divide—let’s discuss how to teach history in ways that build bridges, not walls. Thoughts? #BlackHistoryMonth #CommunityUnity

entities.text: Francis Howell School District is failing to follow its own policies, putting ideology over rules and student well-being. Here’s the proof: 1. Human Sexuality Policy 6116 and Regulation explicitly state that staff should not make value judgments on sexuality, avoid conversations about it, and direct questions to parents. Yet, teachers are reading books about transgender surgeries to elementary kids and maintaining private “Pride libraries” in classrooms with books on boys having romantic encounters with boys—recommended as reading projects. This directly violates the policy. 2. Learning Commons Policy 6310 is ignored by allowing age-inappropriate books that clearly violate Missouri statutes (like those promoting explicit content) and the district’s own guidelines on educational suitability. 3. In-Classroom Library Policy (under 6310/6341) requires all books to be provided in a list to the board for review and prohibits bringing in books not already in the district library. This isn’t happening—unauthorized books are everywhere, the superintendent knows, and nothing’s being done. 4. Transgender Progress flags are hung in multiple classrooms violating Policy 6242 Religious or Controversial Issues. Parents, demand accountability! Contact the board and superintendent today at Board@fhsdschools.org. #FHSD #SchoolAccountability #ProtectOurKids Policy Links: • Human Sexuality Policy 6116: https://go.boarddocs.com/mo/fhsdmo/Board.nsf/goto?open... • Human Sexuality Regulation: https://go.boarddocs.com/.../Reg%206116%20-%20Human... • Learning Commons Policy 6310: https://go.boarddocs.com/.../P6310%20-%20Learning... • In-Classroom Library Policy (under 6310/6341): https://go.boarddocs.com/.../P6310%20-%20Learning... • Policy 6242 Religious or Controversial Issues: https://go.boarddocs.com/mo/fhsdmo/Board.nsf/goto?open...

entities.text: Link to the full book challenge list below! I’m deeply concerned about inappropriate books in our school libraries. I proposed a compromise: move them to an opt-in section for parents who want access, sparing others from challenging titles one by one. Sadly, there’s no middle ground—decisions are polarized, favoring one viewpoint while sidelining conservative parents and those with moral/religious concerns. This list, compiled by many concerned parents, was submitted by just one due to doxxing and harassment risks. We need better dialogue and respect for all perspectives! All books verified and located in the district via the online library.

entities.text: Attention Parents of Francis Howell North Students: Just a heads up (in case you missed it in ENews) – Sexual Abuse Prevention presentations from The Child Advocacy Center of Northeast Missouri are scheduled during English classes on the following dates: • February 3 • February 4 • February 5 • February 10 • February 11 • February 12 • April 13 • April 14 • April 15 • April 16 • April 17 I had the chance to review a private preview of the presentation materials beforehand, which informed my perspective. While I fully see the value in programs like this for educating on abuse prevention and empowering teens with knowledge about consent and boundaries, parts of it—like statements emphasizing that “every person has their own personal boundaries and consent,” and discussions that seem to normalize sexual relationships among teens—left me not 100% comfortable. It’s not about dismissing the program’s intent; it’s about highlighting that parents might want a say in how these sensitive topics are introduced, especially if it doesn’t align with their family values. I personally will be allowing my child to participate. For questions, concerns, or to get an opt-out form, please reach out to Dr. Erin Steep at erin.steep@fhsdschools.org or (636) 851-5031. Website: https://www.cacnemo.org/ Keeping you informed!

entities.text: One more excellent reason to get out and VOTE APRIL 7th! St. Charles County, MO SB 3 – Missouri Property Tax Truth SB 3 does NOT raise taxes It lets local voters decide whether to freeze or cap property tax increases on primary homes A YES vote = stopping automatic tax hikes from rising home values Some school officials are urging a NO vote. entities.text: WAS TRANSGENDER INSTRUCTION GIVEN TO VERY YOUNG STUDENTS WITHOUT PARENT CONSENT? Last night it was reported that a teacher allegedly has violated Board Policy 6116 (Human Sexuality) by discussing transgender-related topics with a very young audience. While board member Sarah Oelke quickly tries to dismiss in attempt to discredit THE TRUTH WILL COME OUT! Listen here: https://youtube.com/.../UgkxKJRO6uYAwk6si4g6v2IwL8hVQLh0B... This policy is explicit and unambiguous: Human sexuality instruction may not occur without prior parent notification and consent. That safeguard exists for a reason — to protect children and to respect parents. So the questions are simple and fair: • What are the ramifications for violating this policy? • How did this happen inside a classroom? • And most importantly — what concrete steps will the district take to ensure this never happens again? Parents should not have to discover policy violations after the fact, through their children. Transparency matters. Policies matter. And when they are broken, accountability must follow. Take Action: Email or call these decision-makers and demand they stop violating policy and protect our children: Chief Academic Officer Glenn Hancock – Glenn.Hancock@fhsdschools.org | (636) 851-4036 Superintendent Mark Delaney – mark.delaney@fhsdschools.org | (636) 851-4000 t

entities.text: SCHOOL CHOICE good or bad? Governor Mike Kehoe says..“Again, open enrollment is not about weakening public education,” said Kehoe. “It’s about strengthening it because when families have choices, schools are pushed to innovate. They’re pushed to improve and respond to the needs of the students they serve.” Rep. Kem Smith, D-Florissant, a longtime teacher, said open enrollment would not improve school quality. “Open enrollment creates winners and losers,” she said. “I know that this body is looking for a way to improve education, to hold schools more accountable. Open enrollment is not the answer.” What grade do you think Francis Howell would get?

entities.text: How Parents Can Check Their Child’s School Library (FHSD) Step 1: Go to the online library https://fhsdschools.follettdestiny.com/portal/portal... • Once on the catalog screen, change Location to “Francis Howell Schools” to search the entire district (Ref: Screenshot 1) ⸻ Step 2: Search • Use Keyword (recommended) • This allows you to search by topics or themes, even if you don’t know a specific title or author ⸻ Step 3: Review results • Look for “Interest Level” (ex: Elementary, Middle, Young Adult) • This can help you question whether the content fits your child’s age (Ref: Screenshot 2) ⸻ Step 4: Click “Details” • Read the summary/description of the book (Ref: Screenshot 3) ⸻ Step 5: Click “Copies” (top right) • See which schools currently have the book (Ref: Screenshot 4) ⸻ How to Challenge a Book • First, contact your child’s building principal • If needed, complete the district’s official review form and submit it as instructed Book Challenge Form https://resources.finalsite.net/.../Review-of-Learning... Ref: Learning Commons Policy 6310 https://go.boarddocs.com/mo/fhsdmo/Board.nsf/goto?open... Ref: Challenged Policy 6341 https://go.boarddocs.com/mo/fhsdmo/Board.nsf/goto?open... You can submit the completed form to the superintendent as listed on the document.

entities.text: It’s CENSORSHIP. Voters should be paying attention. Instead of removing the inappropriate material, they’re now trying to rewrite policy to silence the only board member fighting for our kids innocence—effectively stripping a duly elected board member of her First Amendment rights. Let that sink in. Sexually explicit and wildly age-inappropriate books continue to be allowed in Francis Howell Schools (elementary included!). When school board member Jane Puszkar tries to shine a light on this—by reading the actual content aloud at board meetings and speaking out on conservative talk radio—the response from the mostly liberal board isn’t accountability. Rather than protect children or respect parents, the Francis Howell School Board is willing to go to unbelievable depths to cover their shame and suppress the truth. This isn’t about politics anymore. It’s about free speech, transparency, and protecting kids. Parents should be outraged. Voters should be paying attention.

entities.text: Ashley Goodwin Equal access matters, but a school-issued Chromebook isn’t the only (or safest) way to provide it. Proving to only families in need would be cost efficient and logical. Monitoring school Wi-Fi doesn’t cover off-network use, personal accounts, or apps students add themselves. A family smartphone is parent-controlled; a district device is not.Most classes no longer issue a full set of physical textbooks, so the backpack-weight comparison doesn’t hold. The real differences are distraction, screen time, content students can reach, and how much visibility parents actually have.

entities.author: Shannon Senzig
entities.text: Julie Layton They don't have to be "big books like back in the day," though. That's a false dichotomy. Those books were designed with longevity in mind. They were expected to last for 15 years, so they were hardbound and huge. As a result, lots of schools had to make due with damaged, old, and out of date books that the students had to copy from. What we need are smaller, paperback, single use work books for each student. These have always been around, but the hardbound mega-books were thought to be cheaper so most school districts went that route, with maybe the exception being spelling. Remembering hand copying all those math problems and grammar lessons into a notebook? And pages and pages of wasted space full of illustrations and fluff to justify making the book as expensive as possible? That was completely unnecessary and not what was best for kids. Meanwhile, subjects that do require a text such as science and social studies can be done online in the classroom and study guides can be sent home instead.

entities.author: Shannon Senzig
entities.text: Ashley Goodwin I don't want my kid to have "equal access" though. I don't want my kid to have any access to porn, to social media, to websites trying to steal their identity, to AI generated psychology. I don't want them playing video games at school. I want them reading well-curated literature and quality texts. I want them learning to write, spell, and do math with their hands as EVERY study ever done shows that this is the best method for brain development and retention of skills. What good is "equal access" if what is being accessed is garbage? Ideally, all kids would be exposed to a high quality education, but absent that option, I'm fine with my kid have different access than other kids.

entities.text: No. School staff have zero authority to privately discuss a minor’s sexuality or gender identity without the parents’ knowledge and consent — period. Staff also cannot make value judgments about human sexuality.Teachers are not substitute parents.

entities.author: School Watchlist
entities.text: JD Kunkler I agree full medical transitions are rare. And inattentive parents are usually the ones with vulnerable children. However, it still doesn’t make it right. There is a real institutional push to create secrecy and treat parental opposition as harm.The main route is social transition first. Schools and counselors change the child’s name, pronouns, and facilities under “affirmation” policies — often without telling parents. This isn’t theoretical. It’s documented policy in multiple states and districts, and parents have sued over it.Medical steps (blockers, hormones) are harder to hide, but pathways still exist: clinics that prioritize the minor’s identity and delay parents, one parent acting against the other, or activist networks steering kids around parental consent.Minors don’t pay for this themselves. The money comes from Medicaid or insurance in some states, activist grants, crowdfunding, or one parent funding it in secret.Calling concern over this a “dog whistle” is not accurate. This is a warning.

entities.author: School Watchlist
entities.text: JD Kunkler Jesus ate with sinners to call them to repentance, not to affirm their sin (Mark 2:17). Loving my neighbor includes speaking truth in love - believe it or not I do care about these people. I pray for them nightly, but I believe what they’re doing is evil and needs to be called out. It’s hard to sound “loving” on FB, especially when protecting children from age-inappropriate ideology in public schools.The School Watchlist isn’t exclusion—it’s transparency for all parents. Schools should stay neutral on contested sexual/gender issues instead of pushing one side with flags, curricula, and events. That doesn’t stop anyone from practicing their faith; it prevents schools from undermining mine and parental rights.I don’t have a planks in my eye about this —that scripture means “don’t be a hypocrite”. And parental stewardship isn’t ‘superiority’; it’s obedience (Proverbs 22:6, Ephesians 6:4). We can love people while refusing to let public institutions confuse kids on biology and God’s design.

entities.author: Jonah E Tate
entities.text: School Watchlist I disagree. I think educators have to tailor themselves to each student, because each student comes from very different homes and backgrounds. When taking ed courses at Truman, this was addressed and taught. Every decision, from the curriculum to the setup of the classroom, reflects a set of values. Seeing and experiencing other beliefs around you isn’t indoctrination; it’s a part of life. By separating ourselves from one another, and labeling people different than ourselves as “others” or an outsiders we aren’t protecting these kids from having “beliefs forced on them”, we’re helping them see it as something different or wrong. it’s not the compassion jesus taught. Seeing how diverse our country and state is, is part of the beauty of the US. Embrace diversity, and it won’t feel so different. As educators we should embrace every child’s differences, and tailor our classroom and teaching styles to their needs. Whether that’s a need for a more hands-on learning with projects, a need for lunch assistance for a child, or a child feeling confused about their identity and needing a safe space. We should always give that to them because in the end, we are there for them.

entities.author: Bryan Medlin
entities.text: The Francis Howell School District has an obligation to treat all students and staff with equal dignity and respect — and that includes LGBTQ+ students and educators who are part of this community every single day. The selective removal or suppression of content that represents certain groups, while allowing others, is not neutral — it is a policy choice, and it sends a message.One has to wonder: if this were a religious or faith-based activity, would it have even been questioned? The inconsistency in how content is treated depending on the group involved is impossible to ignore, and it raises serious concerns about whether this district is applying its standards fairly and equitably across the board.I want to recognize Board of Education member Sara Dillard, who has shown the kind of principled, inclusive leadership this district desperately needs. Her attendance at the St. Charles Gay Pride event is a powerful example of what it looks like when an elected official truly shows up for all members of their community — not just the ones it’s comfortable or convenient to support. This is the standard we should expect from every elected official, every teacher, and every principal in this district. Representation and visibility from those in positions of authority matters deeply to students who are watching and looking for someone to stand in their corner.To the rest of the district’s leadership: I am a Francis Howell graduate, and I expect better. Every child in this district — regardless of who they are or who they love — deserves to feel that their school stands with them. I urge you to examine your decisions carefully and ask whether they would hold up to a standard of true equity. The community is watching !!!

Parents, stand firm. Churches, speak truth. Live and let live is one thing—forced celebration of sin is another.God’s Word is our standard, not cultural pressure. Pray for those in deception, but do not bow.#BiblicalTruth #StandFirm #LoveDoesNotAffirmSin

entities.author: Jane Puszkar
entities.text: I don’t believe that Kehoe is going to sign SB1002. However if he doesn’t veto it , then SB 1002 will become law. If he vetoes it then that means their request for MORE money will be placed on Next April‘s ballot. The good news about not signing is that Steven Blair and Carolie Owens do not get an extra 18 months in office and they will both go through an election process next April. I hope everyone is paying attention. They will be asking to be voted back in and at the same time, have their hands in your pocket for more money. Nobody in their right mind would vote them back in especially after the superintendent debacle. Stay tuned Saint Charles. We’ve got a county to save.

entities.text: EMAIL TEMPLATE To: jwelby@stdominichs.org; email@mshsaa.orgDear MSHSAA Board of Directors,As a concerned Missouri parent, I am writing to demand the immediate removal of the question “How does your child identify?” (or any similar gender identity language) from the MSHSAA Preparticipation Physical Evaluation forms.This question has no place on a sports physical form. The only relevant medical information is sex assigned at birth — period. Introducing subjective “identity” language into a required medical clearance document is inappropriate, medically unnecessary, and highly offensive to many families who expect these forms to focus on objective health and safety, not ideology.Missouri law clearly requires participation in school sports based on biological sex. This wording undermines that law, confuses the process, and erodes parental trust. It signals that biological reality is optional — opening the door to unfair competition, including boys in girls’ sports.I urge you to revise the forms without delay to reflect biological sex only. Parents across Missouri are watching and will hold the Board accountable.Thank you for your prompt attention to this critical issue.Sincerely,

As someone who went through Public (K-4) and Private (5-12) you will see the same issues either way.

entities.author: Elizabeth Davie
entities.text: Question: shouldn't parents know what the content is before they challenge it? These are just blurbs about a book. I could write a blurb about the movie "Mrs Doubtfire" like this: "Daniel Hillard was in a tough spot. The terms of the divorce made it clear that he would have no unsupervised time with his children. But when he saw an ad for a nanny for his children, he knew he'd do anything to get his children back. Even if it includes disguising himself as a safe and sweet elderly woman, running an elaborate ruse, lying to his children, and even harming his ex-wife's new boyfriend. What would you do when you lose the ones you love?"I've read "A Long Way Down." Not only is it long-form poetry, a genre that many students would not otherwise be exposed to, but it goes into the mind of a young preteen/teen who has been put in an impossible position through no control of his own and must decide what is right and what is wrong for himself. It's great to think that all kids are always innocent, but that simply isn't true. Reading books about characters that they can relate to is an incredibly meaningful way to start making sense of things that have happened that are beyond their control and a safe way to help kids who are fortunate enough not to have experienced hard things to develop empathy. Also, the philosophical questions that arise from books about war and dystopian societies and some of the other subjects above can be a creative, engaging, and eye-opening path to explore critical thinking.

entities.author: Christen Pierce
entities.text: When I had the opportunity to sit on the review committee for this video, I was grateful for the chance to participate in FHSD’s materials review process. I’m commenting here because I find it very disingenuous to claim that it was “voted to retain by a full liberal committee” when the “full committee” did not return to participate in the vote. On the day that we met to discuss and vote on the video, I was surprised to see that (still active at the time) School Board Director Jane Puszkar did not join us to discuss her concerns about the video, if she had any. It is important for our community to note that choosing not to participate does not mean conservative voices were left out of the discussion. I have five kids and I care deeply about the things they are exposed to; in this case, I do believe that retention was the right choice. If you have any genuine questions about why I voted the way I did, I’m happy to discuss my thoughts about it.

entities.author: Lindsey Scheller
entities.text: Just FYI: when my son was in fourth grade, he had recently been diagnosed with dyslexia and was falling behind in reading. As a mom and as a teacher, I was devastated. I hired Mrs. Becky Hormuth as a tutor for him over the summer. Let me tell you some of the ways she “influenced him.” ￼She taught him a bunch of reading strategies. ￼She made him feel more confident as a reader. She convinced him that being dyslexic was nothing to be embarrassed by. She got him hooked up with high interest books that encouraged him to read more. She made it fun so he wanted to go see her, even over the summer. She made him believe that he was capable of anything he wanted to do. And now he’s a thriving ninth grader with a A in English class. This post is gross.

entities.author: Megan Dolphy Terrell
entities.text: You make this sound like it's required reading for kindergarten, but it's a standard middle school short story. Middle school and high school literature classes have a lot of pieces that make these 12-18 year olds think critically and that dangers can exist. Edgar Allen Poe, The Lottery, and Twilight zone scripts all have "scary" aspects. And all of them are so not realistic that I have never known a kid to be scared by them. Realistic fiction where best friends move away, dogs die, and parents get injured or leave effects kids more! But all of these kinds of literature helps people learn how to be better problem solvers, deal with difficult times, and develop as a better person with stronger emotional regulation. And they learn these things without having to actually live through the trauma. It's actually a very positive thing.

entities.author: Anelise Mossinghoff
entities.text: Prop RT may seem to be a good thing, until you look beyond the short-sighted rhetoric in favor of this. Look at the bigger picture...Think of it this way ...what would you say if your employer said that you will have a pay freeze forever going forward? What would you do about cost of living increases? What about inflation? How will you make up for those increases? It will be impossible. This is what Prop RT will do to the community. Prop RT will devastate schools, fire departments, etc...and any other organization that relies on property taxes for their funding. Where will the shortfall come from? Although Prop RT is not claiming to totally get rid of income tax, one of the suggestions is to increase sales tax. This will make those struggling with buying groceries or ANY goods and services increasingly more difficult to sustain themselves. See the picture below.

entities.author: Libby Settle
entities.text: Conversations about moving towards 1:1 device pushes in today’s day and age continues to baffle me. A quick search shows districts who have had this model are moving away from a 1:1 device often transitioning from "take-home" models to "in-class only" use or scaling back for younger students.Wake County Public School System (North Carolina): The district is moving to end its 1:1 take-home program for its 160,000 students, citing unsustainable long-term costs and the need to prioritize facilities.Fresno Unified School District (California): Starting in 2026, roughly 40,000 elementary students must return their laptops to be used exclusively at school.Charles County Public Schools (Maryland): Beginning in the 2025–26 school year, the district is overhauling its technology approach by shifting to shared devices for elementary grades and restricting individual devices to in-school use only for grades 3–8.Arlington Public Schools (Virginia): This district has scaled back its iPad program, ending take-home access for certain grade levels to reduce screen time and address parent concerns.Denver Public Schools (Colorado): While maintaining some technology, the district has significantly cut hundreds of ed-tech tools to save money and reduce data vulnerability.Kansas School Districts: Select schools in Kansas have ended individual Chromebook assignments specifically to combat excessive screen time. The concerns listed in this post are valid and utilize a considerable amount of a budget that can be reallocated to school repairs, teacher retention, updated curriculums, etc.

entities.author: Karen Sieve
entities.text: I question your motives, Lauren, and of anyone running for a seat on a public school board like Francis Howell when you ignore the fact PropRT (originally SB 3) will hurt St. Charles County public schools, libraries, fire departments, ambulance services, and the developmental disabilities board. Given inflation and continued growth of our county and local municipalities, drastic cuts will be necessary. It’s irresponsible for you to suggest that sales taxes will not increase in the future. The money has to come from somewhere. The Governor also has plans to cut income taxes, and last year, Missouri eliminated capital gains tax. The Governor is also using state funds for private education vouchers, which I assume you, Jane Puszkar, and David Jaworski support as well given your campaigns are funded by the St. Charles Republican Party. If PropRT is passed, sales taxes will increase, and if the Governor eliminates income tax, sales taxes will skyrocket and be regressive, meaning the elderly, the poor and middle class will bear the burden of the higher prices at the grocery store. Services like haircuts, lawn care, etc. will be taxed. What about prescription drugs?So maybe you should practice what you preach about transparency so the community knows that you really don’t support public schools. Vote NO on PropRT. Save our public schools.

entities.rawObservedText: The TRUTH is we’re protecting their innocence. There is NO SHAME in that. SET BOUNDARIES with your child’s SCHOOL!
entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | Normalize keeping your children away from children who are too exposed Normalize keeping your kids away from children who are too exposed. In today’s world, there are kids with full access to the internet, social media, mature shows, and things their little minds shouldn’t have to process yet. And honestly… it shows. My boys are 6, 5, and 3, and sometimes my husband and I wonder if we’re sheltering them. But the truth is, we’re protecting their innocence. We don’t want them learning things that are far too heavy and too mature for their developing brains. Normalize saying no. Normalize not letting your young children be alone with other children, even “good kids,” simply because you don’t know what those kids have seen, heard, or experienced. This isn’t about judgment, it’s about safety. I was a child who was exposed to way too much, way too young. And I can say, it stays with you. It shapes you. It affects you in ways you don’t even recognize until much later. So if you’re the parent who chooses to limit access, supervise closely, set boundaries, and protect your child’s childhood..you’re not overreacting. You’re not controlling. You’re being a present, aware, loving parent. Protecting their innocence isn’t sheltering. It’s parenting. | oLuxraRklv.com

entities.text: TOMORROW ON AIR! When: Tomorrow at 7:00 a.m. Where: KFTK‑FM “97.1 FM Talk” in the St. Louis area. Attention parents, community members, and supporters of our kids at the Francis Howell School District: I’m honored to join school board member Jane Puszkar tomorrow morning on the The Marc Cox Morning Show to speak out against explicit books in our school libraries. We believe our children deserve safe, age-appropriate learning environments, and we’ll be discussing why explicit content in school libraries is a serious concern, what many parents are seeing, and how we can work together for strong standards. entities.text: Big win today — another parent has stepped up and contacted Congressman Bob Onder’s office. His team responded and agreed to escalate the issue, bringing much-needed visibility and light to what’s happening in the Francis Howell School District. Who is Bob Onder? Bob Onder is now the U.S. Representative for Missouri’s 3rd Congressional District (as of January 2025). He has positioned himself as a leading voice defending parental rights, opposing what he calls the “radical gender ideology,” and working to block gender interventions on children. ⸻ What you can do right now: 1. Speak out — submit public comments to your school board and local leaders. board@fhsdschools.org 2. Contact Congressman Onder’s office — ask him to continue pushing for protection of children and to bring pressure to bear on FHSD. Justin.Camp@mail.house.gov 3. Share this post — let more parents and voices step in. 4. Attend school board meetings — demand transparency, accountability, and parental control of curriculum. We are shining a light. We are making them hear us. Let’s do this together.
