entities.text: Student Walk out UPDATE- Email from the district: let’s hope they follow their own rules February 12, 2026 FHN families: Some FHN students made the decision to leave their classes after 3rd period and walk out of the school building. FHN administrators are with the students and are directing students to move to a supervised location on campus. We are being told the walkout is a demonstration against recent actions by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The District has provided guidance to all schools for navigating student protests. Our ultimate goal is to maintain a safe and secure school campus and to ensure that students do not present a major disruption to the learning environment. Here is some information about how we respond to student walkouts. We do not dismiss schools for walkouts, peaceful protests, or other demonstrations. Students who choose to participate in the walkout will be under adult supervision while on campus. Students will receive absence marks based on their actual attendance in each class, and they will face consequences for non-attendance or tardiness consistent with our normal procedures. Instruction will continue as scheduled. Students will not be given additional time to complete quizzes or exams that may be given during the walkout. Should a walkout happen during lunch, students who choose to participate will not be granted additional lunchtime. Consistent with MSHSAA bylaws and the FHSD Activities Handbook, students must attend school the entire day, or be marked excused by the principal, in order to participate in practices, rehearsals, or games for athletic teams or performance groups. Any verbal escalations, inappropriate behaviors, altercations, or other actions stemming from participation in the walkout will be subject to disciplinary action in accordance with the FHSD Code of Student Conduct. Students will be instructed to return to class as soon as the walkout concludes. Members of the media or general public wishing to observe or participate in the student-led walkout will not be permitted on campus during the instructional day. The principal has the authority to temporarily limit all traffic in and out, including parents and visitors, to protect student safety. Administrators and counselors will be available to assist students in processing their emotions. Every effort will be made to be consistent in our guidelines and consequences. The same policies and Code of Student Conduct that govern our work every day will also apply during any student walkouts. Thank you for helping us maintain safe learning environments for all students. FHN Admin Team

entities.attachmentSummary: ShowMe | BOOK ALERT The book: Amazons, Abolitionists, and Activists: A Graphic History of Women’s Fight for Their Rights by Mikki Kendall Library: Francis Howell Central Is marketed as a history of women’s rights. In reality, it is a progressive, intersectional feminist narrative that reframes the entire story through modern identity politics. It uses a classroom framing device to walk readers through history while pushing a clear ideological agenda. This book contains: • Explicit inclusion of LGBTQ rights and gender ideology as core parts of “women’s rights” • Promotion of reproductive rights / abortion as a central women’s issue • Intersectional framing that elevates race and identity politics above classical equality or biblical views of men and women • Criticism of early women’s suffrage leaders (including white feminists) for not being progressive enough on race and other modern causes • A strong call to ongoing leftist-style activism presented as the natural continuation of the fight for rights • Adult political content delivered in an accessible graphic novel format aimed at teens If your child is in Francis Howell Central and checking out graphic histories, this is one worth previewing yourself. Not every book with “women’s rights” in the title is teaching the same values. IMPORTANT FOR PARENTS: If you do NOT want your child to have access to this type of content at school, you must contact your school's media specialist (librarian) or your child's principal. Written notification is required. Without it, your child will have full access to any book the school deems appropriate, even material such as this. You can also: • Request a list of books your child has already checked out. • Sign up to receive daily email notifications of every book your child checks out. These options are available at both the elementary and secondary levels. I've said this before, and I'll say it again: we no longer live in an age where adults are protecting children from sexual content. We are living in an age where adults are offering minor children books with age-inappropriate sexual content under the guise of education. I will never stop fighting for our children because every single one of them are worth fighting for! Students will be instructed to return to class as soon as the walkout concludes. Members of the media or general public wishing to observe or participate in the student-led walkout will not be permitted on campus during the instructional day. The principal has the authority to temporarily limit all traffic in and out, including parents and visitors, to protect student safety. The same policies and Code of Student Conduct that govern our work every day will also apply during any student walkouts. entities.text: Warning Non-binary pronouns being taught in Spanish class (FHSD North HS) Non-binary pronouns are absolutely tied to gender identity — that’s not even up for debate. Non-binary pronouns (they/them, ze/zir, xe/xem, etc.) are directly connected to gender identity. Gender identity is how a person understands and experiences their own gender (male, female, both, neither, or somewhere in between). Pronouns are a way language reflects and respects that identity in everyday communication. So when you are teaching students non-binary pronouns, you are, in fact, teaching about gender identity. That is precisely what our policy prohibits. Send concerns to Superintendent mark.delaney@fhsdschools.org and Helene.Herauf@ed.gov to update the open Dept of Education Complaint OCR 07251345

Non-binary pronouns (they/them, ze/zir, xe/xem, etc.) are directly connected to gender identity. Gender identity is how a person understands and experiences their own gender (male, female, both, neither, or somewhere in between). Pronouns are a way language reflects and respects that identity in everyday communication. So when you are teaching students non-binary pronouns, you are, in fact, teaching about gender identity. That is precisely what our policy prohibits. Send concerns to Superintendent mark.delaney@fhsdschools.org and Helene.Herauf@ed.gov to update the open Dept of Education Complaint OCR 07251345
